messages:
Dev Patel: seeing an early beta customer (EU-only) suddenly getting denied on /v1/chat. Error code `RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH`. They say “nothing changed” but started right after we enabled residency enforcement flag for their org yesterday.

Dev Patel: pasted from their screenshot (redacted):
```
HTTP 403
{
  "error": {
    "code": "RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH",
    "message": "Request region 'us-east' is not allowed for this organization. Allowed regions: ['eu-west'].",
    "request_id": "req_01JMB3A9V3R7..."
  }
}
```

SupportBot: New escalation draft created by Dev Patel (internal) • Suggested tags: data-residency, beta, blocking

Owen Phillips: do we know what endpoint they’re hitting? This is the one where they used the US base URL in their CI last time.

Dev Patel: they claim they’re using the “default” endpoint from our Python snippet. I asked for their exact base URL + SDK init.

Liam O'Rourke: this is the EMEA pilot I’m tracking (TAM). Their security team expects strict EU processing (no fallback). If it’s config mismatch, we should reply with a tight checklist + a quick fix.

Owen Phillips: triage checklist I’ve been using:
1) Confirm org residency policy (pinned vs allowed) in Console screenshot
2) Confirm request host (api vs eu api)
3) Confirm SDK client config `region=` or `base_url=` (some apps override env var)
4) Grab `request_id` + approximate time
5) Check audit event `residency.violation` for decision reason

Owen Phillips: If they’re pinned eu-west, any call to us-east endpoint should 403 before model execution. Expected.

Dev Patel: :thumbsup: will respond with that. Also — what’s the correct EU hostname we want them on? I always forget if it’s `eu.api.redwoodinference.com` or `api.eu-west.redwoodinference.com`.

Brian Murphy: it’s `https://eu.api.redwoodinference.com` for hosted. (Dedicated varies by cluster, but this one is Hosted). If they’re using SDK, easiest is set `REDWOOD_REGION=eu-west` or explicitly `base_url`.

Brian Murphy: also important: the error is 403 by design, but message should include remediation + docs link. If their payload doesn’t include docs_url, send me the `request_id` and I’ll check if they’re on the older middleware version.

Amara Diallo: +1. At gateway we deny on admission and tag the decision. If you can get me `request_id` I can look up the gateway log line and confirm the `resolved_region` vs `policy.allowed_regions`.

Dev Patel: got it. Customer just replied with the snippet they run:
```
from redwood import Redwood
client = Redwood(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"])
resp = client.chat.completions.create(
  model="redwood/llama-3.1-70b",
  messages=[...],
)
```
And their env has `REDWOOD_BASE_URL=https://api.redwoodinference.com` set in prod (US). They didn’t realize.

Owen Phillips: there it is. Answer: switch base URL to EU, or remove it and set `REDWOOD_REGION=eu-west` (if their SDK version supports). Also note that when policy is enabled, we do NOT cross-region fallback.

Liam O'Rourke: can we give them language: “This is expected behavior under residency pinning; request was blocked before processing; no data was processed/stored in US”? That’ll calm the security team.

Brian Murphy: yes. The deny is pre-execution. If they need evidence: we can point them to audit log exports showing `residency.violation` with reason `endpoint_region_not_allowed` and the request_id.

Ethan Park: fyi we had one staging issue last week with stale policy cache, but this sounds like pure endpoint mismatch. Still, send request_id and org id and I’ll sanity check policy evaluator output.

Dev Patel: request_id `req_01JMB3A9V3R7QW0J2K...` (redacted), time ~09:12 UTC. Org is pinned `eu-west` per Console.

Amara Diallo: pulled it up. Gateway log shows:
- ingress POP: us-east
- resolved endpoint region: us-east
- org policy: allowed_regions=[eu-west], pinned_region=eu-west
- decision: deny
- reason: `REGION_NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_ENDPOINT`
So everything working as intended.

Mina Haddad: from routing side: with pinned_region we won’t route across regions even if there’s capacity elsewhere. So changing base URL is required.

Dev Patel: ok, drafting customer reply:
- You’re pinned to EU (eu-west)
- Your prod is calling the US endpoint via env var
- Update to `https://eu.api.redwoodinference.com` (or set SDK region) and retry
- Confirmed request was blocked before processing; no cross-region fallback; audit events available

Owen Phillips: include a quick “how to verify” step: curl health check to EU base URL or print `client.base_url` on startup.

Brian Murphy: also advise they remove the global `REDWOOD_BASE_URL` if they deploy multi-env. We’ve seen it leak from shared Helm values.

Liam O'Rourke: once they confirm, I’ll follow up with their security contact and offer sample audit payload if needed.

Dev Patel: sent. Will monitor for response.

Dev Patel (later): update — customer confirmed switching base URL to `eu.api...` resolved immediately. They asked why it “suddenly started” last night. I explained enforcement beta flag turned on + they previously were silently routed.

Mina Haddad: good. For the record: previously some traffic might have been served in US if they hit US endpoint. Now it’s deterministic deny.

Ethan Park: please file a tiny follow-up: we should make Console surface “Your current SDK/endpoint appears to be US” warning if we detect repeated violations. Might reduce these.

Dev Patel: will do. Logging this as a support learnings note + linking in our escalation playbook. :white_check_mark:
